Module Contents¶

jam.utils.codec.decorators — Codec Generation¶

Automatic codec generation for Python classes.

Decorators¶

  • codable(): Generate codec for class

  • with_codec(): Attach specific codec

  • decodable_dataclass(): Generate codec for dataclass

Type Resolution¶

Basic Types:

bool -> BooleanCodec
int -> IntegerCodec
str -> StringCodec
bytes -> BytesCodec
None -> NullCodec

Container Types:

Array[T,N] -> ArrayCodec[T]
Vector[T] -> VectorCodec[T]
Dict[K,V] -> DictionaryCodec[K,V]
Option[T] -> OptionCodec[T]
BitSequence -> BitSequenceCodec

Custom Types:

@codable -> Generated codec
Codable -> Existing codec

Implementation Details¶

Codec Generation:

@decodable_dataclass
@dataclass
class Point:
    x: U32 # A Codable type
    y: U32 # A Codable type

# Generates:
class PointCodec(Codec[Point]):
    def encode_size(self, value: Point) -> int:
        return 8  # 2 * sizeof(u32)

    def encode_into(self, value: Point, buffer: bytearray, offset: int) -> int:
        pos = offset
        pos += u32_codec.encode_into(value.x, buffer, pos)
        pos += u32_codec.encode_into(value.y, buffer, pos)
        return pos - offset

    def decode_from(self, buffer: bytes, offset: int) -> Tuple[Point, int]:
        pos = offset
        x, read = u32_codec.decode_from(buffer, pos)
        pos += read
        y, read = u32_codec.decode_from(buffer, pos)
        pos += read
        return Point(x, y), pos - offset

Error Handling:

# Type validation
if not hasattr(cls, '__annotations__'):
    raise TypeError("Class must have type annotations")

# Codec resolution
if field_type not in BASIC_CODECS:
    raise ValueError(f"No codec for type {field_type}")

# Field access
if not hasattr(value, field_name):
    raise AttributeError(f"Missing field {field_name}")

Examples

Basic usage:

@decodable_dataclass
@dataclass
class Point:
    x: U32 # A Codable type
    y: U32 # A Codable type

point = Point(1, 2)
encoded = point.encode()  # -> [01 00 00 00 02 00 00 00]

Container types:

@decodable_dataclass
@dataclass
class Container:
    items: Vector_U32  # A custom Vector[u32]
    name: Option_String  # A custom Option[String]

container = Container([1, 2], "test")
encoded = container.encode()
# -> [02 01 00 00 00 02 00 00 00]  # items
# -> [01 04 74 65 73 74]           # name
